audit.whatIsWrong: diffRating and carryRating were empty strings while breakdown.difficulty and report[14] both state 6/10 and 6/10.
audit.why: Blank rating fields render an empty badge against prose that already gives the numbers. Enum fields, exempt from the length band. 50.11% over 870 games supports EVEN.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven side tokens contradicted their own why-lines. whys[0] 'You out-poke Zac at Level 1' and whys[1] 'your Q and E still beat his blob throws' sat above tokens reading 'Zac'; whys[2] and whys[3] say the lane tilts to Zac above 'Skill' tokens; whys[4] says 'Level 6 is even' above 'Dr. Mundo'; whys[6] says 'it's a skill wash' above 'Dr. Mundo'.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is [Dr. Mundo, Dr. Mundo, Zac, Zac, Skill, Dr. Mundo, Skill] and matches whys[] on every single row. The chart had been overwritten with the generic 'lose early, own late' template — which here is backwards at both ends: Dr. Mundo wins Levels 1-2 before Zac's CC chain exists, and the late game is a wash between two unkillable tanks.
audit.corrected: Six flips as one atomic group across both layers, plus the five phases[].why lines that asserted the opposite of their corrected side, plus the window lists.

audit.whatIsWrong: Dr. Mundo's passive is never connected to Zac's kit, and Unstable Matter appears nowhere on the page.
audit.why: Restating the mirror audit from Dr. Mundo's side: every commit tool Zac owns is a displacement — Stretching Strikes throws, Elastic Slingshot knocks up, Let's Bounce! knocks up four times. Dr. Mundo's passive absorbs the FIRST immobilizing effect that hits him and drops a cannister. So the first knock-up in every Zac engage is free, and the cannister on the ground is a heal the player must walk over. That is the single most useful fact in the lane and it was on neither layer. Separately, Unstable Matter deals a percentage of MAXIMUM health as magic damage on a 5-second cooldown — against a Heartsteel/Warmog's build that scales with your own itemisation, and neither armour nor the recommended Plated Steelcaps touches it.
audit.corrected: report[5].t rebuilt around the passive absorbing his first knock-up; spikes[0].text now carries both the passive interaction and Unstable Matter's percent-max-health damage; breakdown.cooldowns lists Unstable Matter at 5s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Elastic Slingshot was listed as 16s in breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].
audit.why: It is 21/18/15/12/9. At rank 1 that is 21 seconds — the longest punish window in the lane and precisely why Dr. Mundo owns Levels 1-2 — and maxed it is 9 seconds, half the figure the page gave. Neither number was right.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[11] said 'Let him eat blobs' but never mentioned the revive.
audit.why: Cell Division does two separate things: it sheds reabsorbable chunks on ability hits, AND on fatal damage Zac splits into four bloblets and revives if any survive. The page only described the first. Walking away from a 'kill' is how this lane gets thrown, and the mirror audit flagged the same passive as the entry's biggest gap.
audit.corrected: report[11].t now names the revive and tells the player to stand on the bloblets.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two ability names were slightly wrong, as the packet flagged: 'Stretching Strike' (should be Stretching Strikes) in spikes[0] and 'Let's Bounce' (should be Let's Bounce!) in spikes[1].
audit.why: Both are genuine near-misses, not false positives — confirmed against packet.enemyAbilities.
audit.corrected: Both corrected in the rewritten spikes text.

edits.before: Your worst level in the game — base stats lose every straight trade. Throw Infected Bonesaw from max range, last-hit, and conserve the health pool Zac wants to chip.
edits.after: Your health pool and a free Infected Bonesaw out-poke him here — Zac has no CC chain until he owns points in both Q and E. Poke, last-hit, take the short trade.

edits.before: Still Zac's window. Heart Zapper absorbs a chunk of burst and pays it back — take only the trades where your W can cash its damage store.
edits.after: Still yours. Heart Zapper absorbs a chunk of his damage and pays it back — take the trades where your W can cash its store inside 325 range.

edits.before: Q ranks make the cleaver chunk real HP and your passive regen ramps. Zac must kill you through the sustain or watch you out-scale — most can't.
edits.after: His grab-into-knockup chain is fully online and his blobs heal back your cleaver chip. Concede these levels, farm from range, wait for first item.

edits.before: Maximum Dosage online — dives and all-ins flip when you press R mid-fight and regen half your HP. Force Zac to commit, then out-last the commit.
edits.after: Maximum Dosage heals through his solo poke, but Let's Bounce! is a collapse tool, not a duel tool. Even alone — lethal the moment his jungler shows.

edits.before: Warmog's makes you a raid boss: full HP between every fight. Zac needs Grievous Wounds and a jungler to even slow you down — split, soak, win.
edits.after: Both of you are unkillable and neither deletes the other. He becomes a teamfight engager, you a frontline sponge — teams decide it, not the 1v1.

edits.before: Zac's Q Stretching Strike double-grab plus E knockup gives him CC you can't answer once he has points in both; he pulls you into his W and E for a real trade. His passive blobs let him heal back your Q chip, so his sustain matches yours through this window.
edits.after: Zac's Stretching Strikes (Q) double-grab plus Elastic Slingshot's knock-up give him a CC chain — but your passive absorbs the FIRST of those and drops a cannister, so it is the second one that lands. Unstable Matter then burns percent-max health, which armour does not touch.

edits.before: Zac R Let's Bounce is a repeated knockup that's built for ganks and dives, not solo kills on you. Your R Maximum Dosage heals through his poke, so a solo fight is even, but his ult makes any jungle collapse deadly.
edits.after: Let's Bounce! is four bounces of knock-up and slow on 120s at rank 1, built for collapses rather than solo kills. Your R heals through his poke, so a duel is even — but any jungler arriving alongside it is lethal.

edits.before: - Zac Elastic Slingshot (16s): matchup-defining — His engage. Punish the cooldown. Track it before every commit. - Your ultimate: spend it on kill windows, never on waves. - Summoners: track his Flash after any close call — it changes every dive call.
edits.after: - Zac Elastic Slingshot (21s at rank 1, 9s maxed): his engage — punish that long early cooldown. - Unstable Matter (5s): percent-max-health magic, so armour does nothing about it. - Your ultimate: kill windows only. - Track his Flash after a close call.

edits.before: Track Zac’s Elastic Slingshot (16s): His engage. Punish the cooldown. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Your passive absorbs his first knock-up and drops a cannister — walk over it, then fight him without it.

edits.before: Let him eat blobs. Get E-knocked-up. Extend into his Q pull. Treat your ultimate as a verdict, never as harassment.
edits.after: Let him eat blobs — or worse, walk off after a kill: his passive revives him from surviving bloblets. Stand on them.

notes: Mirror reused: zac__drmundo had already established that Dr. Mundo's passive eats the first displacement and that every Zac commit tool is one. Restated from this side — the cannister is a free heal the player must walk over, and it is the second knock-up that actually lands. Ratings are inverse to the mirror's and the sides now agree with it. The chart itself was backwards at both ends: Dr. Mundo wins Levels 1-2 (Elastic Slingshot is 21s at rank 1 and the CC chain does not exist yet), and 2+ items is a wash, not a Dr. Mundo window.
